1: The homepage introduces coaching for CA, CMA, CS, CUET, CLAT, IPMAT and UGC-NET, with classroom, live online and recorded delivery. Featured links lead to CA, CS, CMA and Tally/GST. Separate CUET, CLAT, IPMAT and UGC-NET panels describe faculty, study resources, practice tests, flexible delivery and claimed results. A career-after-Class-12 video covers CA, CS, CMA, ACCA, CUET, CLAT and career choice; the career-choice bullet occurs twice. Institution history, an award photograph, rank holders, values, selections, scholarship, mentors, YouTube and student testimonial images follow. Values include tests, revision notes, counselling, an app, individual SWOT analysis, library and transport. The scholarship commemorates Lt. CA Sunil Kumar Agarwal; it supports commerce/professional study through financial assistance and counselling, including students moving into Class 11 and Class 12 commerce/non-commerce students. Faculty images identify Richa Agarwal, Jyoti Madan, Babusha Agarwal, Manish K Singh, S K Garg and Sarika Khanna. A placeholder paragraph remains below the award heading. Student achievements and testimonials are largely image-based; their embedded text was not transcribed.
2: Explains the CA qualification, finance/accounting/tax/audit responsibilities, ICAI regulation and the Foundation, Intermediate and Final stages. Advertised coaching features include professional faculty, institute-aligned materials, practice exams, revision, three delivery modes and claimed first-attempt success. Benefits include individual doubt support, progress tracking, mentoring, notes, career advice and placement help. Target audiences are exam candidates, commerce graduates and professionals seeking tax, audit or corporate-law knowledge. Includes a rank-holder section. Five FAQ topics cover Foundation entry after Class 12, an estimated 4–5-year completion period, coaching versus independent preparation, online/recorded resources and claimed above-average pass performance. No numerical success rate is supplied in the FAQ.
3: Tabs cover introduction, syllabus and FAQs. The page presents four 100-mark papers: accounting, business law, quantitative aptitude and business economics. Quantitative allocation is mathematics 40, reasoning 20 and statistics 40. Accounting coverage includes principles, policies, standards, journals/ledgers, trial balance, cash/subsidiary books, corrections, bank reconciliation, inventories, depreciation, bills/promissory notes, sole traders, nonprofits, incomplete records, partnerships/LLPs and companies. Law covers regulatory framework, Contract Act 1872, Sale of Goods Act 1930, Partnership Act 1932, LLP Act 2008, Companies Act 2013 and Negotiable Instruments Act 1881. Quantitative topics include ratios, equations, finance mathematics, permutations, progressions, sets/functions/calculus, series, directions, seating, relationships, data, probability, distributions, regression and indices. Economics covers demand/supply, production/cost, markets, cycles, national income, public finance, money, trade and India. Nine FAQs address provisional registration after Class 10, Class 12 admission/exam conditions, four-month preparation, result regularization, updated fees/syllabus, registration, material ordering and free ICAI classes. Historical January 2021 and May/June 2021 dates coexist with 2025 examples. Several syllabus entries repeat; one regulatory-framework line contains stray markup. Includes an enquiry area.
4: Introduces CA Intermediate and online ICAI registration after Foundation. Tabs cover overview, syllabus and FAQs. The main structure gives two groups of three 100-mark papers: advanced accounting; corporate/other laws; taxation; costing; audit/ethics; financial/strategic management. Tax and financial/strategic management are each split 50/50. Accounting includes standards 1–5, 7, 9–19, 20–29 as applicable, disclosure, assets/liabilities, revenue, consolidation, company accounts, cash flow, buybacks, amalgamation, reconstruction and branches. Law includes company formation/securities/deposits/charges, administration, dividends/accounts/audit, foreign companies, LLP, General Clauses Act, interpretation and FEMA. Tax covers income, deductions, losses, withholding, returns and GST transactions/compliance. Costing includes materials/labour/overheads, activity costing, costing systems, job/process/service costing, standards, marginal costs and budgets. Audit covers planning, controls, evidence, documentation, reports, banks and ethics. Finance covers funding, ratios, capital costs/structure, leverage, investment, dividends and working capital; strategy covers environments, choices and execution. FAQs state direct-entry thresholds of commerce 55%/other graduates 60%, Foundation 50%, three-year articleship, four-year registration and ₹400 revalidation. The FAQ instead describes eight papers; Paper 5 names also conflict within the page. Includes enquiry.
5: Introduces the last CA level, with overview, syllabus and FAQ tabs. Six papers are grouped into reporting, advanced finance, advanced audit, direct/international tax, indirect tax and integrated business solutions. Reporting covers Ind AS, financial instruments, consolidation, financial analysis, ethics and technology. Finance covers policy, risk, investments, securities, portfolios, securitization, funds, derivatives, foreign exchange, international finance, interest risk, valuation, restructuring and startup funding. Audit spans quality/planning/evidence/reporting, assurance/reviews, digital/group/bank/public-sector audits, internal/forensic work, ESG and ethics. Direct tax covers income, deductions, entity assessment, planning, digital transactions, administration, disputes, anti-abuse, audit, nonresidents, treaty relief, rulings, transfer pricing and BEPS. Indirect tax covers GST supply/credit/registration/invoices/returns, imports/exports/refunds, enforcement, appeals/rulings and customs/foreign-trade policy. Integrated solutions lists company/securities/economic laws and strategic cost/performance management, lean methods, revenue/profit management, reporting, transfer pricing, standards and cases. FAQs state both Intermediate groups plus completed/nearly completed three-year articleship, ten attempts and online-only admit cards. The detailed Paper 3 heading differs from the overview. The enquiry area retains a Foundation label.
6: Defines the CS role in governance, statutory compliance, legal management and board advice, under ICSI. Describes the entrance, Executive and Professional stages. Coaching features include CS/legal faculty, syllabus materials, mock tests/revision, classroom/live/recorded learning and claimed outcomes. Benefits include doubts, mentoring/tracking, notes and career/placement support. Audiences include exam candidates, commerce/law graduates and corporate-management professionals. FAQs describe Class 12 entry, an estimated 3–4-year pathway, structured coaching, online resources and careers in compliance, corporate advisory, legal consultancy and independent practice. The page uses both CSSET and CSEET and retains CA-oriented wording in some section headings.
7: Entrance-course page uses CSEET in its main title and CSSET elsewhere. Tabs are overview, syllabus and eligibility. It says entrance clearance became mandatory from 3 February 2020, subject to exemptions. Four papers are listed at 100 marks each: communication, accounting, economic/business environment, and business law/management. The first three are labelled subjective; the fourth OMR. Communication includes English, correspondence and business terminology. Accounting includes concepts, recording, reconciliation, depreciation, sole-trader accounts, partnerships/LLPs, companies and nonprofits. Economics/business environment is split 50/50 across markets, income, budget, finance, India, entrepreneurship, government/global context, environmental governance, AI and corporate governance. Law/management splits 60/40 across company/contracts/partnership/LLP/sale/negotiable-instrument law and management principles/functions. Eligibility says Class 12 passed/appearing students qualify and graduates/postgraduates must also pass. Listed exemptions are CS Foundation without fee and ICAI/ICMAI Final with ₹5,000. Paper 4’s explanatory objective refers to current affairs and listening/writing rather than its listed syllabus. Enquiry retains a Foundation label.
8: The URL names CA Executive, but the page is CS Executive. Overview, syllabus and FAQ tabs accompany an introduction to ICSI’s revised curriculum. Source describes a second-stage, offline examination held in June and December, with seven papers, objective case questions/descriptive questions, three hours and 100 marks per paper. Group 1 covers jurisprudence/interpretation/general law, company law/practice, business establishment/industrial/labour law, and corporate accounting/financial management. Group 2 covers capital markets/securities, economic/commercial/intellectual-property law, and tax. A single FAQ describes enrolment after entrance clearance or exemption, including graduates/certain professionals. That exemption description differs from the entrance page’s graduate statement. Enquiry retains a Foundation label.
9: Introduction refers to the 2025 curriculum and December 2025 exam. Tabs cover overview, syllabus and FAQs. The syllabus lists seven papers in two groups: ESG, drafting/pleadings, compliance/audit/due diligence, elective 1, strategy/corporate finance, restructuring/valuation/insolvency, and elective 2. First elective choices cover CSR, internal/forensic audit, IP law, AI/data/cyber law, advanced tax and IFSCA regulation. Second choices cover dispute resolution, GST/corporate tax planning, labour, banking/insurance and insolvency. The overview simultaneously describes three modules and nine papers. Four FAQs give a commerce 55%/other degree 60% threshold plus Executive clearance, identify changed topics, mention age 17 for Executive before Professional, and refer readers to ICSI. These are source statements requiring review rather than verified admission advice. Enquiry retains a Foundation label.
10: Describes cost/management accounting, finance, taxation, corporate law and strategic business work; stages are Foundation, Intermediate and Final. Promotes syllabus resources, practice/revision, three delivery modes, claimed outcomes, doubt support, mentoring, notes and career/placement help. Audience includes candidates, commerce graduates and tax/finance/strategy professionals. FAQs describe Class 12 entry, a 3–4-year course estimate, coaching support, online delivery and roles including cost accounting, analysis, strategy, tax and CFO. Source names the Institute of Cost Accountants using ICAI, describes Company Secretaries/legal professionals as faculty and asks an online-CS question on this CMA page. These cross-course labels are retained as observations.
11: Foundation introduction mentions Class 12, twice-yearly exams and ICMAI; source also calls the pathway Certified Management Accountant. Tabs cover overview, syllabus, eligibility and FAQs. It cites the June 2025 syllabus and discontinuation of the 2016 scheme. Four papers cover law/communication, financial/cost accounting, mathematics/statistics and economics/management. Topics include contracts/sales/negotiable instruments, accounting fundamentals/special transactions/final accounts/costs, arithmetic/algebra/business calculus, data/averages/probability/indices/time series, markets/money/banking/business environment and management. Eligibility text lists Class 10 and senior-secondary/equivalent routes, commerce/rural-service diplomas, reciprocal CS Foundation exemption and CA Intermediate-related exemptions; it also mentions the old Common Proficiency Test. Four FAQs state four papers, unlimited attempts through revalidation, retaking only a failed subject and mandatory three-year articleship without exemption. The overview and eligibility wording need reconciliation; FAQ claims are not independently validated. Enquiry retains a Foundation label.
13: Tally/GST landing page promotes TEPL training, including computer applications, programming diplomas, office automation, publishing, Excel, DTP and web design, and claims more than 24,000 learners. Features include English/Hindi teaching, practical work, online assessments, original software, verifiable certification and availability to commerce/non-commerce students. Institute/online delivery is advertised alongside professional guidance, counselling, app, library and placement opportunities. Certification benefits include career progression, Tally-authored materials, GST-oriented software, job-portal access, digital certification and online assessment. The catalogue links to Office Automation; Master Accountant; GST Simulation certification; payroll/income tax; inventory; TallyEssential; TallyProfessional; online internship; GST; TDS; GCC VAT; international Essential/ACE; and Oman Essential. GCC VAT is listed twice. A qualified-professionals image section follows. The Office Automation link uses an online-internship slug; the actual internship has a separate -2 slug.
14: Despite its online-internship URL, the displayed course is Office Automation. It teaches Windows 11 and Word, Excel and PowerPoint for workplace/accounting tasks. Five chapters cover computer components/hardware/software and desktop settings; files/folders, wildcards, recycle bin and Notepad; Word documents/paragraphs/Insert functions; Excel formatting/references/formulas/logical and financial functions/lookups/Goal Seek/charts/pivots; and PowerPoint startup/templates/presentation completion. Chapters end with conclusions, takeaways and exercises; shortcuts are included for the introductory chapter. An enquiry area is associated with Tally/GST.
15: An accounting/finance/taxation programme for manufacturing, trading and services combines TallyPrime work, GST simulations, online internships and employability training. Eight modules have assessments of 120, 120, 30, 60, 60, 60 and 30 minutes, followed by a 40-hour internship assignment. First accounting module covers fundamentals, Tally setup/records, banking/reports/security/data, inventory, receivables/payables/orders/purchase costs, cost centres/budgets, GST/TDS and financial-year changes. Advanced module covers currencies, interest, job work/costing, banking, Tally.NET, advanced GST/TDS, TCS and payroll/tax. Other modules cover basic English/grammar; GCC VAT; GST tutorials/assignments; Windows/Word/Excel/PowerPoint; and personality skills. Personality topics are interpersonal skills, decisions, group dynamics, conflict, leadership, time, emotional intelligence and stress. The internship module repeats those personality chapter names rather than specifying accounting role assignments. Includes Tally/GST enquiry.
16: Explains a practice environment modelled on GST-portal activity, including registration, uploading invoices, e-way bills, e-invoicing and returns such as GSTR1. Combines TallyPrime certification with simulated compliance work. Eligible linked course labels are TallyEssential Level 3, TallyProfessional, TallyComprehensive and GST using TallyPrime. Includes Tally/GST enquiry.
17: Payroll/income-tax training using TallyPrime covers salary setup, processing, tax calculation and statutory deductions including PF, ESI and professional tax. It targets HR/accounting/finance work. A single module includes payroll introduction, payroll masters, primary/statutory pay heads, salary definitions, income-tax masters, configuration, payroll processing with tax, payroll reports and statutory reports, ending with a conclusion and quiz. Includes Tally/GST enquiry.
18: Inventory-control training uses business exercises/quizzes to cover stocks, batches, job costing, materials, orders, reorder levels, warehouses/transfers and reports. Five modules cover inventory storage/classification (masters, batch movements, price lists); purchase/sales orders (processing, outstanding orders, reordering and godown transfers); additional purchase costs (transaction configuration); manufacturing/job work (in/out orders and inter-godown materials); and job costing (documents, activation, chart of accounts, transactions and reports). Each module includes learning objectives/introduction, a conclusion and quiz. Careers referenced include operations, accounting, supply chain and business administration. Includes Tally/GST enquiry.
19: Beginner accounting certification is divided into three levels with durations 35, 35 and 36 hours. Level 1 covers accounting fundamentals; TallyPrime installation/company setup; chart of accounts; vouchers; banking/cheques/reconciliation; statements/MIS; security/users; backup/restore; and basic GST transactions/credit/payments/returns. Level 2 covers inventory types/masters/warehouses/batches; bill references, receivables/payables, settlement and credit limits; sales/purchase cycles; added purchase costs; cost/profit centres; budgets/scenarios; printed books/registers; and GST/e-way bills. Level 3 covers advanced GST supplies/returns/composition dealers; TDS setup/transactions/challans/reports; data export/import/ODBC; and company splitting/grouping for the next year. GST simulation provides return, e-way-bill and e-invoice practice. The introductory descriptions of levels differ from the detailed headings: the prose associates payroll/tax/compliance with Level 2 and comprehensive certification with Level 3. Careers include accounting, finance, administration and taxation. Includes Tally/GST enquiry.
21: Advanced certification assumes existing financial-accounting knowledge. Volume 1 covers multicurrency exchange/vouchers/forex differences; simple/compound interest and balances; job-work orders/material transfers; job costing/documents/reports; advanced banking/postdated cheques/e-payments; and Tally.NET remote access, browser reports, synchronization and virtual users. Volume 2 covers advanced GST supplies (SEZ, exports, mixed/composite, reverse charge, advances), invoices/e-way bills/credit/tax/returns; advanced TDS expenses, software, commission, capital/advance payments, reversals, contracts, nonresidents, DTAA, foreign-currency income and reimbursements; government payment, forms 26Q/27Q and TRACES; TCS sales/rates/exemptions/advances, payment and form 27EQ; payroll masters/attendance/income tax; PF, ESI, professional tax, gratuity and returns. An additional GST simulation section describes interactive returns, e-way bills and e-invoices. Includes Tally/GST enquiry.
22: The displayed online-internship course describes practical accounting exposure aligned with NEP 2020, intended to improve conceptual knowledge and job readiness using Tally. Course options listed are TallyEssential Levels 1, 2 and 3, plus TallyEssential Comprehensive. Includes Tally/GST enquiry. This is distinct from the similarly named URL without -2, which displays Office Automation.
23: Specialist Indian GST certification combines theory with TallyPrime compliance. Introductory module covers GST, invoice/e-way-bill concepts, tax calculation order, transactions, credit adjustment/payment, regular-dealer returns/filing, QRMP, composition dealers, sandbox practice and connected e-way bills. Advanced module covers domestic/interstate supplies, unregistered/composition purchases, mixed/composite/exempt supplies, SEZ/other-territory supplies, reverse charge, exports, advances, invoice/e-way reports, credit reversal, payments and electronic returns. GST simulation adds practical return/e-way-bill/e-invoice exercises. Includes Tally/GST enquiry.
24: Specialist withholding-tax certification teaches theory and TallyPrime practice, including varying deduction rates, works contracts/GST, foreign-currency income, ITNS 281 challans and electronic forms 26Q/27Q. Seven learning sections cover TDS fundamentals/capital introduction; activation/masters/group-ledger setup; expenses and multiple deductions; advanced expenses/reversals; works contracts/interest; government payment; and challan/report generation. Includes Tally/GST enquiry.
25: Middle-East taxation/accounting training covers GCC VAT using TallyPrime and business scenarios. Four modules cover VAT fundamentals; purchases/sales and intra/inter-GCC supplies; returns, imports/exports, tax-inclusive supplies, profit-margin transactions and imports for subsequent sales; and invoices/printing, authority payments and filing. Introductory topics additionally mention activation and advance receipts. Readers are directed to locate a partner for enrolment. Includes Tally/GST enquiry.
27: International accounting certification targets Middle-East learners and domestic/cross-border taxation. Eleven modules cover accounting systems/theories/accrual-versus-cash/regulation/statements/inventory; TallyPrime installation/licences/educational mode/company setup; masters/chart of accounts; accounting/inventory vouchers and supply chain; bill-wise receivables/payables/limits/debtor performance; cost centres/categories; purchase/sales orders; final accounts/MIS/drill-down reporting; role/password security, automatic login and TallyVault; backup/restore/data repair; and GCC VAT calculations, transactions, invoices, payments and reports. Source directs enrolment through a certified partner. Includes Tally/GST enquiry.
28: A beginner Middle-East accounting guide uses TallyPrime, practical cases and exercises. Introductory coverage includes installation and company creation. Six learning modules cover accounting fundamentals/double entry/golden rules; ledger/group chart of accounts; stock units/groups/categories/godowns; everyday receipts/contra/payments/purchases/sales/debit-credit notes/journals; bill references/receivables/payables/settlements/credit limits; and financial/MIS reports including trial balance, balance sheet, profit/loss, cash flow, ratios, registers and inventory. Enrolment is directed through a partner. Includes Tally/GST enquiry.
29: Beginner Oman-oriented certification allows individual levels or a comprehensive course. Level 1 has accounting fundamentals (systems, theories/policies/standards, cash/accrual, FASB/GAAP/IFRS, records, statements, corporate/inventory accounting, FIFO/average costs, depreciation and computerized accounting); TallyPrime licences/setup/navigation; chart-of-account masters; business/accounting/inventory vouchers and bank reconciliation; and final accounts/MIS/drill-down reports. Level 2 covers bill-wise receivables/payables, ageing/reminders/confirmations/settlement/credit limits; cost centres; purchase/sales order processes, receipts/delivery/rejections/payments and closure; roles/passwords/TallyVault; and backup/restore/repair. Level 3 covers GCC VAT terminology/registration/supply types/calculation/configuration, domestic/intra-GCC transactions, reverse charge, returns/services/unregistered suppliers/tax-inclusive amounts, English/Arabic/bilingual invoices, authority payments, reconciliation and return filing. Conclusions, takeaways, shortcuts, exercises and answer keys accompany modules. Introductory outcomes refer to both GST and VAT. Answer-key text repeats at the end. Includes Tally/GST enquiry.
30: ACCA page gives duration 1.5–3 years; classroom/live/recorded modes; registration/subscription/exam fee categories; placement assistance; recognition in 180+ countries; founding year 1904; 257,900 members; 530,100 prospective members; 64,000+ jobs; and master-level benchmarking. Target audiences include Class 12 students, commerce/finance and other graduates, finance leaders and mobile professionals. Entry claim: 65% English and mathematics/accounts, 50% other subjects; repeated twice. Knowledge papers are BT/MA/FA; Skills LW/PM/TX/FR/AA/FM; compulsory professional SBL/SBR; choose two AFM/APM/ATX/AAA. Exemption table gives exams/exemptions: Class 12 13/0; commerce graduate 9/4; M.Com 9/4; both CA IPCC groups 8/5; CA 4/9. Promotes 25+ years, full placement assistance, professional teachers, 4.9/5 Google rating, materials/mock tests/flashcards and networking. Career cards include accounting, UK tax (repeated), management accounting, forensic/external audit, audit assistance, transfer pricing, mergers/acquisitions, risk, treasury and business analysis. Contact call-to-action follows.
31: CLAT page describes law admissions through a consortium and claims 24 NLUs. Overview/syllabus/eligibility/FAQ tabs precede a table claiming 150 questions/marks in two hours, English language and -0.25 errors. Row figures: English 28–32, current affairs 35–39, legal reasoning 35–39, logical reasoning 28–32 and a malformed final row 13–17; one cell contains an unrelated personal name. Topic coverage includes comprehension/vocabulary/grammar, current/static affairs, legal propositions/cases/contracts/torts, arguments/puzzles/logic, arithmetic/algebra/geometry/data/probability/mensuration. Claimed weights are 20–25%, 25–30%, 25–30%, 20–25% and 10–15%. Eligibility states Class 12, 45% general/OBC/PwD/NRI/PIO/OCI and 40% SC/ST, no upper age, and Indian/overseas categories with foreign-national rules. FAQs cover 6–12 months’ preparation, offline 2026 exam, marks/age, online applications, Class 12 rather than XI and photograph/signature/reservation/domicile uploads. Includes enquiry, incorrectly associated with Foundation.
32: CUET introduction describes a 2022 central-university entrance system, NEP context, standardized access and rural inclusion. Tabs cover overview/syllabus/eligibility/FAQs. Structure claims IA language, optional IB language, up to six domain subjects and general test. The source says 13 languages but lists 15: English, Hindi, Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu. Language coverage includes comprehension, writing, grammar/vocabulary and literature. Commerce domains cover accounts/statements/partnerships/companies/nonprofits/ratios/cash flow; business environments/organizations/enterprises/finance/marketing/HR; micro/macro/Indian economics; and algebra/calculus/statistics/commerce mathematics. General-test topics include GK/current affairs, logic, quantitative/data/mental aptitude and English. Eligibility claims Class 12 with 50% general/45% reserved, no specific 2025 age ceiling, university-specific conditions and Indian/NRI/foreign applicants. FAQs address definition, three-part preparation, language skills, Class 11/12 NCERT/domain practice, daily GK/reasoning/maths preparation, board marks versus entrance scores and coaching consistency/materials. A general-test question repeats, an accounting heading appears in the language section and calculus topics recur under statistics. Enquiry retains a Foundation label.
33: IPMAT page describes five-year management admission after Class 12 and distinguishes Indore/Rohtak variants. Tabs cover overview/syllabus/eligibility/FAQs. Source gives CBT, 120 minutes, typical QA-MCQ/QA-short-answer/verbal sections, +4 correct and -1 incorrect MCQs. Topics include number systems, arithmetic, algebra, geometry/trigonometry, combinatorics/probability/sets/matrices/progressions, data interpretation; vocabulary/grammar/comprehension/verbal reasoning; and variant-specific seating/relationships/directions/codes/series/input-output/calendars/Venn diagrams. Verbal weight is stated as 25–30%. Eligibility claims passed/appearing Class 12, Class 10/12 aggregates 60% general/OBC/EWS or 55% SC/ST/PwD, English at Class 12, and birth on/after 1 August 2005 for 2025 (1 August 2000 reserved relaxation). Nationality includes Indians/foreign candidates with institute rules. FAQs discuss programme definition, eligibility, sectional cutoffs plus interview/possible writing test and academic composite, non-maths preparation, calculator restrictions and interview importance. Dates and differing institute rules require review. Includes enquiry with a Foundation label.
34: UGC-NET page covers teaching/JRF/PhD eligibility. Source claims NTA delivery twice yearly, CBT, English/Hindi, three hours, +2 correct and no penalty. Papers are 50 questions/100 marks and 100 questions/200 marks, with one/two-hour allocations and 81 subject choices. Paper 1 units cover teaching, research, comprehension, communication, mathematical reasoning, formal/Indian logic, data, ICT, development/environment and higher education; Paper 2 covers postgraduate subject knowledge, with examples English, politics, history, psychology, chemistry, commerce, sociology and law. Eligibility claims master’s 55% or reserved 50%, JRF under 31 and no professor age ceiling. FAQs give fees ₹1,100 general/₹550 OBC-NCL/₹275 SC-ST-PwD-transgender; applications March–April/September–October; claimed qualifying percentages general 40%/50%, reserved 35%/45%; lifetime professor and three-year JRF validity; unlimited teaching attempts but JRF up to age 30; dual applications; final-year study; and education gaps. JRF ages conflict, and the weightage heading has no text table. Includes enquiry with a Foundation label.

Each displays a zero rating/count and an exploration link. Individual card destinations are recorded below; those extra pages were not requested or audited.
